goal: Teacher Kim holds up a big sheet of paper painted all purple in the art corner of the kindergarten classroom. Behind her, a line of small paw prints in many colors goes across the floor. No letters, words, or numbers anywhere.
colorPrompt: Compose one children's book picture from the element pictures. Picture 1 shows four approved characters side by side, left to right: the boy Ben, the girl Nan, Teacher Kim, and the puppy Pip (ignore the gray background and the shadow; for Nan use her own pictures instead, because this one has tiny eye-corner errors). Picture 2 is the empty art corner of the kindergarten classroom: cream plaster walls with dark-brown timber beams, a wooden plank floor, a small window, two wooden easels with blank paper, and a low wooden table with paint pots; use it as the background and keep the same room. Picture 3 shows seven thin sheets of paper, each painted all over in one flat color: red, blue, yellow, green (top row), orange, pink, purple (bottom row); draw only the one sheet this picture needs, as a thin, flat sheet of paper. Picture 4 shows a sheet of white paper with many flat colorful paw prints in seven colors (left), and a strip of wooden floor with one line of eight small colorful paw prints (right); each print is one big round pad and four small toe pads. Keep the soft, round, bright 3D render look of the pictures, not a 2D drawing and no outlines. The children keep their chibi proportions: a big head and a small body. Hands are small, chubby child hands with five clear short fingers (four fingers and one thumb) when open, never fists unless stated, and a hanging hand shows relaxed, separate short fingers. Rendering errors to NOT copy from the character pictures: a tiny dark tick mark or pale skin flap at the outer corner of an eye, and a faint pale crease on a forehead. Each eye ends in a smooth, rounded corner; Nan alone keeps one short, thick, curved eyelash flick at each outer eye corner. Clean eye corners, no streak on the forehead, no marks on the face. The ears are smooth, with one clean rounded rim. Each piece of clothing is one even color with no pale patches, no pale blotches at the shoulders, and no stains. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no writing on any picture or sign. The picture is for young children and is rated G. Keep each character exactly as in the pictures: Teacher Kim: a grown woman, about one and a half times as tall as the children, with medium-length dark-brown hair in a low ponytail, a soft green cardigan over a cream blouse, navy trousers, brown flat shoes, a gentle smile. The picture: Teacher Kim holds up a big sheet of purple paper. A medium-wide shot at a low camera height. Teacher Kim stands in the middle of the art corner (picture 2), faces the camera, smiles, and holds up one big thin sheet of paper painted all PURPLE (the purple sheet of picture 3; draw only that one sheet) in front of her chest with both hands, natural adult hands with five separate fingers at its edges. The whole sheet is in view, flat, plain purple, with no marks. Behind her, ONE line of EIGHT small paw prints in many colors (the strip of picture 4, right side) goes across the wooden floor from the left to the right. There is no puppy and no child in the picture. Exactly the characters named here are in the picture, and no other person or animal. A character of the pictures that this description does not name must not appear. Every named character has a clear, whole, friendly face. The page text is "It is purple." and is context only: do not draw any text.
linePrompt: Picture 1 is a 3D-rendered children's book picture. Convert picture 1 to line art for a student book: thick, even black lines (about three times a normal outline), simple closed shapes that a 5-year-old can color, on pure white. No blush circles, no eyelash ticks, no hair strands, no shading, no gray, no texture lines, no text. Keep every shape in the same place and the same size. Draw each eye as a closed outline with a big solid black pupil (a filled black circle) inside it. Draw the mouth exactly as in picture 1: an open mouth stays an open mouth drawn as a closed outline, and a closed smile stays one curve. Draw each hand as a closed outline with each finger as a separate rounded shape. Each head of hair is one closed shape. The ear is one closed outline with at most one inner curve. No lines on the clothes other than the outline, the collar, and the star. Simplify the background: draw only a few large, simple, closed shapes (the floor line, the wall line, two or three big closed beam shapes, the window as one closed square, each easel as one closed frame, the table as one closed shape, the toy kitchen and the shelf as large closed box shapes). No wood grain lines, no floor plank lines, no plaster texture, no hatching, no tick marks, no small details on the shelf. Every outline is one closed line that never runs into a background line; no loose line ends anywhere. Every line inside an object ends on another line. Use few background shapes. Each painted sheet of paper is one closed rectangle with nothing drawn inside it (the paint color is not drawn).
